extracted.intended_audience: Federal agency officials, administrative law staffs, hearing examiners, agency general counsels, and regulatory statisticians
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and definitions for collecting, classifying, measuring, and reporting statistics on formal administrative proceedings (particularly those involving hearing examiners) and illustrative uniform procedural rules for agencies (computation of time, presumptions, form of decisions, admission/discipline of attorneys, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'proceeding' for the report
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'proceeding' means a matter which in normal course is referred to an APA Sec. II examiner for evidentiary hearing (oral or written presentation) and for a recommended or initial decision, even though it may be a consolidated proceeding involving more than one petition, application, or complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a matter involves several claimants/applicants/respondents but looks toward resolution by a joint hearing and a single decision, it is reported as one 'proceeding.'

rubrics_metrics.name: When a matter is counted as 'commenced' for reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: If hearings are ordinarily afforded on every petition/complaint, the proceeding is counted from the date of initial filing. If hearing is only designated when issues preclude summary administrative determination, the proceeding is counted from the date it is designated for hearing (entry on hearing docket or referral to hearing examiners).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Age of proceeding is computed from the applicable commencement date chosen under the above rules; agencies must apply the appropriate start-date rule depending on their statutory/administrative practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of tables: Part A vs Part B inclusion rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Part A tables include all stages of proceedings (from commencement to final agency disposition) for matters that were pending at any time during the fiscal year. Part B covers only the period a proceeding was in the hands of hearing examiners (from assignment to examiner to termination before the examiner).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part B excludes stages before assignment to examiners and agency consideration after examiner decision (except where a table specifically extends beyond those limits, e.g., Table 12).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions from the report's statistical universe
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceedings where hearings are conducted by the agency itself or by staff other than APA examiners are not included; except that Table 12 may consider examiner employment generally. Proceedings where the examiner merely conducts the hearing and certifies the record to the agency without preparing an initial or recommended decision are generally excluded (except Table 12).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Social Security cases and certain Indian probate matters have particular data availability limitations noted elsewhere; agencies should note such exceptions when reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency-provided 'type of proceeding' categorization
rubrics_metrics.description: The division into types of proceedings is made by the reporting agencies (characterizations are abbreviated for tables).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparisons between agencies or types should be attempted only with full recognition of significant procedural differences among agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table 1 (Backlog and Volume) column definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Columns indicate number of pending cases at fiscal year start (by stage), input during year (new and reopened), output (cases closed), and balance remaining at fiscal year end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grand totals demonstrate aggregate pending, input, output, and end-of-year balance; Social Security cases may dominate totals and should be separately considered when comparing trends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of age-groupings rather than averages
rubrics_metrics.description: Age of proceedings is reported in grouped ranges (e.g., <6 months, 6-12 months, 1-2 years, etc.) because grouped age distributions are considered more indicative than simple average or median figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where age data are not available for categories (e.g., Social Security or certain Indian probate matters), that is noted and such cases are excluded from age analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manner of disposition categories (Table 3 / Table 9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disposition categories include: decided on the merits by agency final decision after examiner/after hearing; decided by agency without initial/recommended decision by examiner; examiner's decision became final without agency review; dismissed or withdrawn without decision on the merits; (separately noted) default, consent, settlement, or compromise dispositions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Percentages and counts for each disposition category are reported; certain agencies (e.g., Social Security) may account for large shares in particular disposition types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall time from commencement to final agency disposition (Table 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure elapsed time from the proceeding's commencement date (per rules above) to the agency's final disposition; report distribution across time ranges (e.g., within 6 months, 6-12 months, 1-2 years, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data may be unavailable for some subcategories (e.g., certain Social Security appeals); percentages of proceedings in each time band should be reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time from commencement to assignment to examiner (Table 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure time between commencement and assignment to a hearing examiner; report distribution (assigned at commencement, ≤1 month, 1–3 months, 3–6 months, 6–12 months, >1 year).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Five agencies assign all proceedings to examiners at commencement (FTC, Social Security Administration, Bureau of Indian Affairs, Office of Alien Property, Coast Guard); Civil Aeronautics Board assigns in safety enforcement proceedings. Agencies should indicate their practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency time under advisement after examiner decision (Table 6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure period from when matter is first ripe for final agency decision (e.g., all exceptions filed, record certified) to issuance of the agency's final decision; report distribution across time bands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data not available for some appeals (e.g., SSA to Appeals Council); report percentage taking ≤3 months, >1 year, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part B Table 7 examiner-processing metrics (backlog/input/output)
rubrics_metrics.description: For matters that were in examiners' hands, report number pending before examiners at start and end of year, new cases assigned to examiners (including remands/reassignments), examiner output, and balance pending at year end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare year-to-year examiner workloads and backlogs; exclude Social Security and other cases when data unavailable or anomalous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length of time pending before examiners (Table 8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure time each proceeding had been pending before an examiner as of June 30 (from assignment date to that date); report distribution including proportion >1 year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data for some categories (SSA, Indian probate) may be unavailable; comparisons should account for such omissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner disposition time (Table 10)
rubrics_metrics.description: For proceedings disposed of by examiners on the merits after hearing, report overall examiner time from assignment to decision and distribution across time bands (e.g., ≤3 months, 3–6 months, >2 years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide year-to-year comparisons (e.g., percentage disposed ≤3 months in 1957 vs 1958).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time under advisement by examiners (Table 11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure from date of final submission to examiner for decision (last proposed findings and brief filed, etc.) to date examiner's decision issued; report distribution (≤1 month, ≤3 months, ≤6 months, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report percentages (e.g., 34% decided by examiners ≤1 month in 1958; 84% ≤3 months).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner staffing and productivity metrics (Table 12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report examiner employment by grade and man-years, average number of days per man-year in hearings and pre-hearing conferences, average number of decisions on the merits per man-year, and number of proceedings assigned for hearing-only certification of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions: a 'day of hearing' is any day an examiner presides over a hearing or conference (full or partial day, one or more proceedings). Man-year figures account for inter-agency loans, separations, and entrances. Average days/decisions per man-year are computed by dividing reported totals by man-years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation of time (President's Conference illustrative rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: When computing any prescribed period, exclude the day of the act/event that starts the period; include the last day unless it is a Saturday, Sunday, or legal holiday, in which case extend to the next business day. If the period is less than 7 days, intermediate Saturdays, Sundays and holidays are excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this uniform illustrative rule unless agency statute or rule provides otherwise; variations among agencies exist and are reported in Appendix Table on computation of time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic extensions / additional days for service by mail or residence
rubrics_metrics.description: Some agency rules provide automatic extension when service is by mail (commonly 3 days added), or additional days for parties/practitioners whose offices are in specified distant geographic areas (commonly 5 days; 20 days for beyond continental U.S.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific agencies vary: NLRB, Indian Claims Commission, Subversive Activities Control Board add 3 days in certain conditions; FCC, ICC, SEC provide 5-day (or 20-day) geographic extensions; one agency limits the 3-day addition to filing-response periods ≤10 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumptions (illustrative uniform rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency may, upon proof of predicate facts without substantial dispute and by direct, clear, and convincing evidence, make certain presumptions (continuity, identity, delivery, ordinary course, acceptance of benefit, interference with remedy) where consistent with surrounding facts and circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presumptions may be made with or without prior request or notice; examples: continuity presumption for facts of a continuous nature, delivery presumption for properly addressed and prepaid mail/express, interference with remedy presumption when party in control destroys or withholds material evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stipulations and admissions of record in multi-party proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: A stipulation or admission of record is conclusively presumed against any party bound thereby and no other evidence on that fact will be received for that party, provided the stipulation is binding and either made on the record at a pre-hearing conference/oral hearing/or filed writing and served on all parties within five days after service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withdrawal of such stipulations/admissions before final decision is permitted upon satisfactory showing of inadvertence or bona fide mistake contrary to the true fact and where withdrawal will not unjustly prejudice other parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and content of decisions (illustrative rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every decision (recommended, initial, tentative or final) should contain, in order: (i) correct caption; (ii) description of nature/status of decision; (iii) separately identified headnotes of points decided; (iv) designation of all parties and counsel; (v) concise statement of nature/background of proceeding; (vi) concise statement of facts (without recitation of evidence); (vii) concise definition of issues; (viii) separately identified paragraphs discussing each issue with principles, reasons and precedents; (ix) statement of rule/order/sanction/relief or denial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The illustrative template aims to promote uniformity and clarity in agency decisions and to ensure decisions state reasons and authorities relied upon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform rule recommendation on admission to practice before agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal that agencies dispense with formal admission procedures and adopt a uniform rule: anyone who is a member in good standing of the bar of the Supreme Court or of the highest court of a state/territory/insular possession/DC and not under court order suspending/disbarring/restricting practice is eligible to practice before the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal appearance or signature on filings in a representative capacity constitutes representation and a representation of authority; agencies should recognize representation and serve notices on counsel where fact is known in writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for disqualification/suspension from practice before an agency
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency may disqualify (temporarily or permanently) an attorney who: does not meet admission requirements; has been disqualified/suspended/disbarred by any other federal agency; is guilty of unethical or unprofessional conduct; or is otherwise not qualified to represent others before the agency. Contemptuous conduct at an agency hearing may be ground for summary suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies maintain rules listing specific grounds; the scope and labeling of grounds vary by agency (see Appendix table mapping grounds across agencies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for discipline of attorneys (investigation through order)
rubrics_metrics.description: General Counsel receives reports/complaints, may authorize investigation, and if formal proceedings are warranted files a complaint with specific allegations; service is made personally or by registered mail; respondent has ten days to answer (may request hearing), default procedures apply, hearing held within 60 days if requested, General Counsel prosecutes charges, and agency issues order with findings/conclusions/disposition; proof standard is preponderance (or prima facie if default).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If disqualified, agency publishes order in Federal Register and notifies state licensing authorities with availability of transcript upon request; hearings may be closed unless respondent requests open hearing; record of evidence must be kept.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service and representation mechanics
rubrics_metrics.description: When a party is represented by an attorney and that fact is known in writing to the agency, notices and written communications required or permitted will be given to that attorney; if a participant is represented by more than one attorney, service upon one suffices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where other statutory service methods exist, they control instead; signature/appearance on paperwork constitutes representation to the agency.
